summary: Misordered function-call delivery after HTTP/2 stream refactor causing out-of-sequence tool side-effects
description:
Issue summary: After the recent HTTP/2 stream refactor in api-gateway (rolled 2026-03-11), several long-running orchestrations that rely on ordered function/tool calls are observing out-of-sequence tool executions. This manifests as earlier tool side-effects being executed after later ones, or occasionally skipped and replayed, causing user-visible duplication or missing state updates.

Impact: Customer AtlasWorks reports inconsistent downstream state for production workflows (payment+fulfillment orchestration). Behavioral impact includes duplicated webhook posts, undo/redo races in their order pipeline, and one customer workflow that resulted in delayed invoice creation. Affects a small cohort (estimated 3% of requests for that tenant) but high-risk for financial flows.

Environment: Dedicated pool for AtlasWorks in prod us-east-1. SDKs in customer stack: python-sdk v0.12.0, ts-sdk v0.9.6. Redwood components implicated: api-gateway HTTP/2 connection pool and http2-proxy path that recently changed stream multiplexing heuristics. Serving runtime shows normal token latency.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer provides a streaming orchestration: model calls that issue tool/function invocations in a sequence (authorize -> reserve -> capture).
2) Client opens a single HTTP/2 stream multiplexed across several multiplexed logical channels (or uses SDKs that multiplex).
3) Mid-stream the connection receives a stream-level RST (simulated network blip) and the SDKs perform a reconnect + retry using the platform backoff policy.
4) On resume, function-call acknowledgements are reconciled; however, ordering is not preserved and callbacks/tools are dispatched out of original sequence.

Expected behavior: After reconnect/resume, function/tool calls from a single logical session should be delivered and/or deduplicated in the original order, preserving transactional sequence semantics where the customer relies on ordered side effects.

Actual behavior: Some tool invocations are delivered out-of-order: later tool runs appear to complete before earlier ones, and occasional duplicates occur when the client-side retry and gateway-level retry both re-dispatch the same logical call. Evidence shows request IDs preserved but the delivery ordering across multiplexed channels changes.

Logs / Observed traces (sanitized):
- gateway: stream-reset for stream_id=4823 cause=GOAWAY; reconnect window start=2026-03-11T15:22:10Z
- customer webhook logs: POST /webhook/orders 2026-03-11T15:22:13Z (capture) then 2026-03-11T15:22:12Z (reserve) -> ordering inverted
- serving-runtime trace: request_id=atlas-ord-7f3 token_latency=42ms model=gpt-redwood-13b serve_node=gpu-12
- sdk-python debug: retry_attempts=2 backoff_ms=[150, 500] resume_session_id=sess-993

Attachments: Customer provided minimal reproduction harness and request transcripts in a private S3 link (shared with support).
comments: 2026-03-13 10:12 - Aisha Fernandez (Support): Customer-reported. Initial triage indicates regression after 2026-03-11 gateway refactor. Asked customer for request transcripts and SDK versions.
2026-03-13 11:03 - AtlasWorks (Customer): Provided transcript and sample orchestration. Noted that issue reproduces ~1 in 30 runs under load. Impact is business-critical for invoicing pipeline.

2026-03-13 15:40 - Evan Chen (SRE): Reproduced a simplified failure in staging by injecting stream-level RSTs against http2-proxy. Observed reordering when multiplexed logical channels resumed. Raising to engineering for deeper analysis.

2026-03-14 09:22 - Marco Li (Gateway Eng): Confirmed change in PR #1892 altered preferred stream owner selection during resume. Potentially reorders queued dispatch across logical channels. Investigating fix and compatibility with SDK resume behavior.
2026-03-14 12:05 - Support (Aisha): Communicated mitigation workaround to customer (disable multiplexing / fall back to per-request connections) while fix in progress.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: New stream owner selection algorithm in http2-proxy can dispatch queued messages from resumed streams in a different ordering across logical channels when stream reset and resume occur concurrently.

Hypothesis 2: SDKs apply local retries and re-emit function calls on reconnect; gateway-level replay/forwarding and SDK retries both send the same call with same request_id but different sequence timing, causing perceived reordering due to race windows.
Reproduction: Created a staging harness that mirrors customer multiplexing pattern (python-sdk v0.12.0 streaming client) and injected RST after 1200ms. Observed ordering inversion in 7/100 runs.

Logs: Gateway queue timestamps show dispatch order changed on resume: queued[callA@15:22:11, callB@15:22:12] -> sent[callB, callA] after resume. SDK ack reconciliation sees both delivered and marks later one first because of channel affinity switch.
Short experiment: Disabling channel-affinity patch in gateway restores ordering in our harness. This narrows scope to the refactor in PR #1892.
Impact matrix: Only multiplexed streaming sessions using per-session resume (not simple request/response) are affected. Dedicated customers with per-request patterns unaffected.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided (2026-03-14): Instructed AtlasWorks to disable multiplexed session reuse in SDK (setting SDK_MULTIPLEXING=off) or use per-call connections for critical flows. Both options reduce throughput but preserve ordering.

Short-term fix (in progress): Gateway engineering to revert or mitigate the stream-owner selection behavior introduced in PR #1892. Patch branch created: revert/stream-owner-affinity-1892. Running integration tests against customer harness.

Long-term action items: 1) Add explicit ordering-preservation tests for multiplexed resume scenarios to CI. 2) Add an opt-in header for customers that require strict in-order delivery during stream resume. 3) Update SDK docs with recommended resilience patterns and idempotency token guidance for orchestrations.
Follow-up: Schedule postmortem and customer-facing incident note after fix rollout. Coordinate with AtlasWorks to validate in their dedicated staging before prod rollout.
